name: French Riviera and the Var: Nice, Menton, Antibes, Saint-Pau

destination.name: French Riviera and the Var: Nice, Menton, Antibes, Saint-Pau
destination.pitch: Four Riviera towns you can string together by train and a Calanques finale that needs a car and a fire map, worth nine days from May to early July or September, and a slog in August.

because.nature: Limestone calanques you walk down into and swim from, red porphyry in the Esterel, Cap Canaille at 394m above the sea, and a coastal path around Cap d'Antibes that closes in a gale.
because.exploration: Perched villages on the Loup, a Friday market in Italy 10 minutes by train, a botanical garden on the border built by a Victorian and a Corbusier housing block with a bar on the roof.
because.food: Socca from a wood oven, Nicoise cooking in a 12-table room with no phone, bouillabaisse for 100 euros a head in the Vallon des Auffes, sardines in Marseille for 15, and Cassis white with sea urchins.
because.relaxation: Sand at Antibes and Juan-les-Pins, a lime tree terrace in Saint-Paul, a Cassis quay at 19:00, and a bay at Villefranche you can swim in before 09:00.
because.culture: Matisse, Chagall, Picasso, Cocteau, Renoir, Leger and Miro each in the building they painted or the town they died in, plus the MuCEM and Le Corbusier in Marseille.
because.adventure: En-Vau on the polished descent, Sugiton with a permit, Cap Roux in the Esterel, the Nietzsche path up to Eze and the Tirepoil rocks in a swell.
because.city: Nice is a real city of 340,000 with a tram, an opera and a port; Marseille is 870,000 people, the second city of France, and the only one on this coast that does not exist for tourists.

destination.caveat: In August the coast road stops, a Nice pebble beach is 3 euros of shade short of unbearable, restaurants take bookings a week out, and the Calanques trails shut on any day the prefecture paints the massif red at 18:00 the evening before. Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

cities.name: Nice
cities.base: Vieux Nice for the market, socca and the old-town bars at your door, accepting noise until 01:00 in summer; the Port Lympia side or Place Garibaldi if you want quieter streets and a 10 minute walk to

cities.name: Villefranche, Eze and the Corniches
cities.base: A day, not a bed. Villefranche is 8 minutes from Nice by train, Eze is 25 minutes by bus 82 or a train to Eze-sur-Mer and 450m of the Nietzsche path on foot, and the Cap Ferrat villas hang off the sam

cities.name: Menton
cities.base: The old town or the streets around the Halles and the Bastion, so the covered market, the Cocteau museum and the beach are 300m apart. Garavan, the last bay before Italy, is quieter and 20 minutes on

cities.name: Antibes and Juan-les-Pins
cities.base: Vieil Antibes, inside the ramparts within five minutes of the Cours Massena market, where the sand beach of La Gravette is a two minute walk; Juan-les-Pins is 25 minutes across the neck of the Cap on

cities.name: The Esterel and the Corniche d'Or
cities.base: A red volcanic massif between Cannes and Saint-Raphael with the coast road running under it. Agay and Theoule have hotels but the walk is a morning and the drive is the rest, so do it as a day from An

cities.name: Saint-Paul-de-Vence and the perched villages
cities.base: Inside or just outside the ramparts of Saint-Paul, so you have the village after the coaches leave at 18:00 and the Fondation Maeght 15 minutes up the hill on foot. Vence, 4km north, is a working town

cities.name: Cassis
cities.base: Within 500m of the port. The Calanques trail leaves from the west end of town, the boats from the quay, the market from Place Baragnon, and in summer you cannot drive in past the Gorguettes car park a

cities.name: Calanques National Park
cities.base: 20km of limestone coast between Marseille and Cassis with no beds except a youth hostel at La Fontasse with no electricity. Walk in from Cassis for Port-Miou, Port-Pin and En-Vau, or from the Luminy c

cities.name: Marseille
cities.base: The Vieux Port side of Le Panier, or the 6th and 7th arrondissements toward the Corniche, so the fish market, the MuCEM and the Saint-Victor stairs are on foot and bus 83 runs you along the sea to the

outings.name: En-Vau from Cassis, via Port-Miou and Port-Pin
outings.why: Three calanques in a row: the boat-lined inlet of Port-Miou at 20 minutes, the pine-shaded pebbles of Port-Pin at 45, and En-Vau at about 90 minutes each way with a steep polished descent that is worse coming up at 15:00. No water, no shade
outings.season: All year; 1 June to 30 September only on days the prefecture
outings.fallback: Port-Pin and back, two hours, or the 5-calanque boat from the quay when the massif is red.

outings.name: The Calanques boat from Cassis
outings.why: Open boats from the Cassis quay run 3, 5, 8 or 9 calanques in 45 minutes to 2 hours for roughly 21 to 33 euros, 40 with a swim stop; they do not land, which is why they sail on red fire days when nothing else moves. Buy at the kiosk on the
outings.season: February to November, hourly in summer, a few a day in shoul
outings.fallback: A kayak from the Bestouan beach into Port-Miou and Port-Pin, about 60 euros for a half day, when the sea is flat.

outings.name: Sugiton from Luminy
outings.why: Bus B1 to the Luminy campus, a forest track to the Col de Sugiton and a rope-assisted last drop to two pebble coves under the Candelle cliff, 50 minutes down and an hour back up in full sun. From late June to the end of August it takes a fr
outings.season: All year; permit 20 to 21 June, daily 27 June to 30 August,
outings.fallback: Morgiou from the same trailhead, no permit, a fishing hamlet with a restaurant at the bottom, or the Belvedere de Sugiton viewpoint at 30 minutes without the de

outings.name: Cap Canaille and the Route des Cretes
outings.why: The 15km cliff road from Cassis to La Ciotat over the highest sea cliff in France, 394m straight down to the water, with lay-bys every few hundred metres. Shut to cars on Sundays and on red fire days, and shut to everyone when the mistral t
outings.season: All year subject to wind and fire closures; check the barrie
outings.fallback: The 20 minute walk to the Port-Miou viewpoint on the Presqu'ile.

outings.name: Frioul and the Chateau d'If
outings.why: Boats from the Vieux Port quay in 20 minutes to the prison island of the Count of Monte Cristo, then on to the Frioul archipelago for a swim in the Calanque de Saint-Esteve and a walk over bare limestone with no shade. The chateau is 7 euro
outings.season: All year; the chateau closes in high wind and the boats in a
outings.fallback: Frioul alone, which stays open on red fire days, or the Corniche Kennedy walk to the Vallon des Auffes.

outings.name: The Tirepoil path around Cap d'Antibes
outings.why: 5km from the Garoupe beach car park along the rocks of the east and south of the Cap to the Villa Eilenroc gate, with steps cut into the rock and steel handrails on the exposed bits. Two hours of walking, no cafe on the way, closed by the t
outings.season: All year; closed in strong wind or swell.
outings.fallback: The Garoupe lighthouse from the Chapelle de la Garoupe car park, 20 minutes up the pilgrim path, and the sand at Garoupe.

outings.name: Cap Roux in the Esterel
outings.why: A loop from the Sainte-Baume car park above Agay to the Pic du Cap Roux at 453m, red rock over a blue sea, about 8km and 3 hours with the Saint-Honorat grotto on the way. The Var regulates its massifs from mid-June to mid-September on a dai
outings.season: All year; October to May is best, summer only on green or ye
outings.fallback: The Corniche d'Or drive alone, stopping at the Calanque d'Anthéor and the Rade d'Agay, or the Ile Sainte-Marguerite ferry from Cannes.

outings.name: Eze and the Nietzsche path
outings.why: Train to Eze-sur-Mer, then the Chemin de Nietzsche 430m straight up a mule track to the village in about an hour and a half, the cactus garden on the castle rock at the top, and bus 82 back down to Nice. The village is one street of shops a
outings.season: All year; the path is exposed and best before 10:00 from Jun
outings.fallback: Bus 82 from Nice to the village and the garden only, three hours, or Villefranche instead.

outings.name: Villefranche and the Cap Ferrat coast path
outings.why: Eight minutes on the train from Nice to Villefranche, a swim off the Marinieres beach before the day-boats anchor, the Cocteau chapel on the quay, then the coast path around Cap Ferrat from Beaulieu past the Villa Kerylos to Saint-Jean, 7km
outings.season: All year; the path can be closed by the mairie after a storm
outings.fallback: Villefranche old town and the beach alone, three hours.

outings.name: Ventimiglia Friday market and the Hanbury gardens
outings.why: The 10 minute train into Italy for the seafront market that runs from 07:00 on Fridays, leather, cheese and focaccia and half of Monaco's housekeepers, then a taxi or bus 1 to La Mortola for 18 hectares of botanical garden falling to the se
outings.season: Market every Friday, garden all year, closed Mondays in wint
outings.fallback: The Hanbury gardens alone on any day, or Ventimiglia Alta, the old town on the hill across the Roya, when it is not Friday.

outings.name: Sainte-Agnes and Gorbio
outings.why: Two stone villages in the hills behind Menton, Sainte-Agnes at 780m with a Maginot fort and a view down to Italy, Gorbio 400m lower with an elm planted in 1713 in the square. 30 minutes by car up hairpins, or bus 10 from the Menton bus stat
outings.season: All year; the Maginot fort opens afternoons only, and in win
outings.fallback: The coastal path from Garavan around Cap Martin to Le Corbusier's cabanon, two hours.

outings.name: Vence, the Matisse chapel and Tourrettes-sur-Loup
outings.why: The Chapelle du Rosaire on the edge of Vence, 7 euros and 30 minutes inside, is the reason to be in this valley; it keeps odd hours, afternoons Tuesday to Saturday for certain, some mornings, never Sunday. Then Vence old town for lunch and
outings.season: All year; the chapel shuts mid-November to mid-December some
outings.fallback: The Fondation Maeght and the Saint-Paul ramparts, which need no car.

places.name: Cours Saleya market
places.note: Flowers and produce Tuesday to Sunday from 06:00, the food stalls packing up by 13:30; on Mondays it is a brocante instead, so do not come for tomatoes on a Monday.

places.name: Vieux Nice on foot, Place Rossetti to the port
places.note: Ochre Genoese streets four storeys deep, the baroque Sainte-Reparate cathedral and the Palais Lascaris; walk it before 10:00 or after 18:00, because from 11:00 to 17:00 in summer it is a single slow queue of people holding ice cream.

places.name: Chez Pipo
places.note: Socca from a wood oven since 1923, 3.50 to 7.50 euros a plate with pissaladiere and a carafe of rose, shared tables and a queue on the pavement from 18:00; closed Mondays, and Tuesdays too outside summer.

places.name: La Merenda
places.note: A dozen tables, stools, no phone and no cards, where Dominique Le Stanc cooks stockfish, daube and beignets de fleurs de courgette for 35 to 50 euros; you book by walking in the day before, and it is shut Saturday and Sunday.

places.name: Bar des Oiseaux
places.note: The old-town bistro locals name when you ask, Nicoise plates and a 3-course lunch under 30 euros, Tuesday to Saturday only and booked out by the weekend; go at 12:00 on a weekday.

places.name: Colline du Chateau
places.note: Free, 93m up, open 08:30 to 20:00 in summer and 18:00 in winter; the artificial waterfall and the view down the Baie des Anges are what everyone comes for, and the free lift from the Quai des Etats-Unis is often out of order, so plan on the Montee Lesage stairs.

places.name: Promenade des Anglais at 07:30
places.note: 7km of blue chairs and pebble beach, worth an hour on foot or a bike before the heat and the traffic; every beach along it is fist-sized grey pebbles, so bring sandals and a mat, and the private clubs charge 25 euros and up for a lounger.

places.name: Musee Matisse
places.note: A red Genoese villa in the Cimiez olive grove with the cut-outs and the Roman arena next door; 12 euros, closed Tuesdays, 10:00 to 18:00 April to October and 17:00 in winter, and bus 5 or 33 from the centre because the walk up is 40 minutes uphill.

places.name: Musee National Marc Chagall
places.note: The 17 canvases of the Biblical Message in the building Chagall designed the light for, 10 euros or 12 during an exhibition, free the first Sunday of the month, closed Tuesdays; 20 minutes on foot from the station and a 15 minute walk from the Matisse museum.

places.name: MAMAC
places.note: Yves Klein blues, Niki de Saint Phalle and the Nice school in four marble towers with a roof terrace over the old town; 10 euros or the 15 euro four-day pass for all the municipal museums, closed Mondays.

places.name: Fenocchio, Place Rossetti
places.note: Nearly a hundred flavours since 1966, tomato-basil and lavender included, 3.50 euros a scoop; the queue at 15:00 in August is 20 minutes, so come at 11:00 or after 21:00.

places.name: Place Garibaldi and the port bars
places.note: Les Distilleries Ideales on the square and the wine bars around the rue Bonaparte are where Nice under 40 drinks; a glass is 5 to 7 euros, the terraces run to midnight in summer, and the old-town Irish pubs 300m away are the thing to avoid.

places.name: Villefranche-sur-Mer old town and the Rue Obscure
places.note: A 14th century covered street and a stack of ochre houses down to a fishing harbour, eight minutes by train from Nice; the Cocteau chapel of Saint-Pierre on the quay is 3 euros and shut Mondays and from mid-November to mid-December.

places.name: Plage des Marinieres
places.note: The one beach near Nice you can call sandy, coarse grey grit rather than pebbles, in a bay deep enough that cruise ships anchor in it; the train runs along the back of it, and by 11:00 in summer there is no towel space left.

places.name: Eze village and the Jardin Exotique
places.note: A medieval rock 430m above the sea with a cactus garden on the castle ruin at the top and a view to Corsica on a clear day; the garden is around 7 to 8 euros and opens at 09:00, and the one street of galleries below it is a shuffle by 11:00.

places.name: Chemin de Nietzsche
places.note: A mule track 430m straight up from the Eze-sur-Mer station to the village, 90 minutes with no shade and loose stone underfoot; start by 08:30 in summer and carry a litre of water each, then take bus 82 down.

places.name: Villa Ephrussi de Rothschild
places.note: Nine gardens on the spine of the Cap with musical fountains every 20 minutes and a pink villa of Fragonards and Sevres; about 17 euros, open daily 10:00 to 19:00 in July and August and 18:00 the rest of the year, and bus 15 from Nice stops at the gate.

places.name: Villa Kerylos
places.note: A 1902 reconstruction of a Greek house on a rock at Beaulieu, marble baths and mosaics, run by the national monuments; about 13 euros, open daily, and the coast path to Saint-Jean starts at its gate.

places.name: Halles Municipales
places.note: Thirty stalls under a 1898 iron roof, 08:00 to 13:00 every day though thinner on Mondays, with barbajuans and socca at the counters for 1.50 to 3 euros and Mitron's lemon tart; be there before 10:00 for the fish.

places.name: Basilique Saint-Michel-Archange
places.note: The baroque church at the top of the ramp from the port, with a pebble-mosaic square in front that hosts the August chamber music festival; generally open 10:00 to 12:00 and 15:00 to 17:00 and shut during services, so treat the hours as loose.

places.name: Musee Jean Cocteau, Le Bastion
places.note: The 17th century harbour fort Cocteau decorated himself with pebble mosaics and his Innamorati drawings, 10:00 to 12:30 and 14:00 to 18:00, closed Tuesdays; the big Wilmotte museum next door was wrecked by a storm in 2018 and has not fully reopened, so this is the Cocteau you get.

places.name: Jardin Serre de la Madone
places.note: Lawrence Johnston's terraced garden of 1924 climbing a valley 2km behind town, restored and half wild; 10 euros, 10:00 to 18:00 April to October, closed Mondays and all of November and December, steep steps throughout, and bus 7 from the bus station.

places.name: Mitron Bakery
places.note: Mauro Colagreco's bakery in the old town, ancient-grain sourdough and the Menton lemon tart, 08:00 to 19:00 Tuesday to Saturday and until 15:00 on Sundays, closed Mondays; there is also a stall in the Halles.

places.name: Le Petit Port
places.note: A shaded garden terrace behind the old port where Menton eats grilled fish and octopus without a view premium, 12:00 to 14:00 and 19:30 to 22:00, closed Tuesday and Wednesday; book in July and August.

places.name: Mirazur
places.note: Three Michelin stars on the last hill before Italy, a tasting menu around 450 euros from the terraced gardens below, Wednesday to Sunday, booked months out on release days; lunch is the same food with the view, and a late cancellation costs 450 euros a head.

places.name: Plage des Sablettes
places.note: The town beach under the old town, rebuilt with a wide promenade; it is fine gravel that photographs like sand and is not, so bring sandals, and the pebble beaches west along the Promenade du Soleil are rougher still.

places.name: Ventimiglia Friday market
places.note: Friday only, from 07:00 along the Lungo Roya and the seafront, said to be the biggest market in Italy; 10 minutes by train from Menton for 3 euros, bags, cheese, focaccia and a plate of pasta for 12 euros before the French crowds arrive at 10:30.

places.name: Giardini Botanici Hanbury, La Mortola
places.note: Sir Thomas Hanbury's 18 hectares from 1867 dropping from the Aurelian Way to the sea, 10 euros, 09:30 to 18:00 in summer with last entry an hour before, closed Mondays in winter only; the walk down is easy and the walk back up in August is not.

places.name: Cap Martin coast path and Le Corbusier's Cabanon
places.note: The sea-level path from Menton's Garavan port around Cap Martin passes Eileen Gray's E-1027 and the 3.66m by 3.66m hut Le Corbusier died swimming from; the huts are guided visits by Cap Moderne, booked ahead, about 20 euros, and the path is free and two hours.

places.name: Monaco for the Oceanographic Museum
places.note: Twelve minutes by train, and the rock with the aquarium is worth a morning, about 20 euros; the casino square, the harbour of yachts and the 30 euro club sandwich are the part to skip, so see the Prince's palace change of guard at 11:55 and go back to Menton for lunch.

places.name: Musee Picasso, Chateau Grimaldi
places.note: The castle on the sea wall where Picasso worked in autumn 1946 and left 23 paintings and 44 drawings, plus a Nicolas de Stael room and a sculpture terrace over the water; 10:00 to 18:00 mid-June to mid-September and split hours the rest of the year, closed Mondays.

places.name: Marche Provencal, Cours Massena
places.note: Under an iron roof, 07:30 to 13:00 and to 13:45 in summer, daily from June to August and closed Mondays from September to May; the goat cheese and socca stalls are the real ones, the lavender-soap end is for the coaches, and craft stalls take over the hall in the afternoons.

places.name: Vieil Antibes and the ramparts walk
places.note: From the Port Vauban gate along the Vauban sea wall past the Picasso castle to the Gravette beach and back through the Safranier quarter's streets; 30 minutes of walls with the Alps behind the bay and the biggest yachts in Europe in the port.

places.name: Plage de la Gravette
places.note: Real sand, a curved breakwater and shallow water two minutes from the market, which is why it is towel to towel by 11:00 in July; the water can be murky after a storm and there is no shade at all.

places.name: Plage de la Garoupe
places.note: The Cap's sand beach where the Murphys raked the seaweed for Fitzgerald; most of it is private clubs at 30 to 60 euros a lounger, the public strip at the north end is 50m, and Plage Keller is shut for rebuilding until 2027. Bus 2 from the Antibes bus station.

places.name: Sentier de Tirepoil, the Cap d'Antibes coast path
places.note: 5km of rock path with handrails from the Garoupe car park round to the Villa Eilenroc, two hours, closed by the town in a gale; no cafe, no shade and no way off in the middle, so water and shoes with grip.

places.name: Le Vauban
places.note: An old-town dining room with a 49 euro three-course menu of veal with Nicoise vegetables and panisse, service 12:00 to 14:00 and 19:00 to 21:30, closed Monday and Tuesday; the kind of place that is full of Antibes families on a Friday.

places.name: La Petite Escale
places.note: Ten tables and a fixed menu built on the morning's fish from the Antibes boats, bream ceviche and monkfish; closed Monday and Tuesday, and in summer you book or you do not eat here.

places.name: Maison de Bacon
places.note: The bouillabaisse house on the Cap since 1948, open daily 12:00 to 14:00 and 19:00 to 22:00, with a 69 euro three-course lunch and the bouillabaisse itself well over 100 euros a head; the terrace faces Antibes and the Alps, and the rooftop bar from 18:00 Wednesday to Sunday is the cheap way in.

places.name: Absinthe Bar
places.note: A vaulted cellar under the market with 1900s fountains, hats to borrow and a piano on Friday and Saturday nights; 8 to 12 euros a glass, hours are unreliable, and one is enough.

places.name: Juan-les-Pins beach and the Pinede
places.note: Fine sand facing west for the sunset, mostly private clubs with a free strip at the Pinede end; the pine grove hosts Jazz a Juan for ten days in mid-July, tickets 40 to 120 euros, and outside the festival the town is a 1960s resort of ice cream and Vespas.

places.name: Marineland
places.note: Closed for good in January 2025 after the orca law; still on maps and in older guides, so do not drive out there.

places.name: Pic du Cap Roux from the Sainte-Baume car park
places.note: An 8km loop with 480m of climb to a 453m summit of red porphyry over the sea, the Saint-Honorat hermit's grotto on the way; the forest road in is barred on red fire days from mid-June to mid-September, and the car park is full by 09:30 on a spring Sunday.

places.name: Corniche d'Or drive, Theoule to Agay
places.note: 30km of coast road cut into red rock in 1903 with a lay-by at every calanque; the Calanque d'Anthéor and the Pointe de l'Esquillon are the stops, the road is one lane each way and August makes it a crawl.

places.name: Rade d'Agay
places.note: A sand beach in a near-closed bay under the red hills, the swim after Cap Roux; the west end near the station is public and the beach clubs at the east end charge 25 euros for a lounger.

places.name: Fondation Maeght
places.note: Josep Lluis Sert's building in the pines with the Miro labyrinth, the Giacometti courtyard and a Braque pool, 18 euros, open every day 10:00 to 18:00 and until 19:00 in July and August; 15 minutes uphill on foot from the village and half the point is outdoors, so avoid the middle of a hot day.

places.name: Saint-Paul ramparts and rue Grande
places.note: A 16th century walled village of one street of galleries; between 10:30 and 17:30 it belongs to the coaches, so walk the walls at 08:00 or after 18:30 when the light goes orange and the shops shut.

places.name: Chapelle Folon
places.note: The White Penitents' chapel repainted by Jean-Michel Folon in 2008, 3 euros for 20 minutes of mosaics and glass, 10:00 to 12:30 and 14:00 to 18:00 daily in season and closed Tuesdays from mid-October to mid-April.

places.name: Cemetery, Chagall's grave
places.note: Chagall is under a plain slab with pebbles on it at the south tip of the village, next to a view down to the sea; free, quiet and open from 08:00.

places.name: Le Tilleul
places.note: The terrace under the lime tree at the village gate, open all day every day from breakfast to 22:00 with the dish of the day from 16 euros and menus at 32 and 39; the sensible lunch in a village that otherwise charges for the view.

places.name: Cafe de la Place
places.neighborhood: Saint-Paul-de-Vence, place du General de Gaulle
places.note: The bar on the boules pitch where Montand played; a pastis at 18:30 watching the old men throw is the cheapest thing Saint-Paul does well, and the food is ordinary.

places.name: La Colombe d'Or
places.note: Lunch under a Leger mural with a Calder by the pool, hors d'oeuvres on the famous trolley and roast lamb, about 90 to 120 euros a head; the food is decent, the walls are the reason, it is booked weeks ahead in summer and it shuts from late October to Christmas.

places.name: Chapelle du Rosaire, the Matisse chapel
places.note: Matisse's last work, white tile, black line and three colours of glass, 7 euros with a room of the studies; afternoons Tuesday to Saturday are certain, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday mornings usually, never Sunday and probably not Monday, and it has shut for a month in late autumn, so check chapellema

places.name: Vence old town and the Friday market
places.note: A real town of 20,000 with a walled centre, a Chagall mosaic in the cathedral and a food market on the Grand Jardin on Friday mornings, smaller ones on Tuesdays; lunch here costs half what it does in Saint-Paul.

places.name: Tourrettes-sur-Loup
places.note: A village on a rock above the Loup that grows violets and sells them candied, 7km west of Vence, with a market on Wednesday mornings and workshops instead of galleries; 25 minutes from Saint-Paul by car or bus 51 from Vence.

places.name: Gourdon and the Gorges du Loup
places.note: An eagle's nest village at 760m with a view over the whole coast from the terrace by the church, reached up the gorge road past the Saut du Loup waterfall; 35 minutes from Saint-Paul by car, one street, and better at 17:00 than midday.

places.name: Musee Renoir, Domaine des Collettes
places.note: The olive-grove house where Renoir spent his last 12 years, his studio and wheelchair intact and 14 canvases; about 6 euros, 10:00 to 13:00 and 14:00 to 18:00 in summer, closed Tuesdays, and 15 minutes downhill from Saint-Paul toward the coast.

places.name: Cassis port and quays
places.note: A fishing port that became a resort in the 1920s, pastel houses and pointu boats under the Cap Canaille cliff; the quays are a promenade at 19:00 with a glass of Cassis white, and the same quays at 14:00 in August are the thing that makes people say the Riviera is over.

places.name: Cassis market, place Baragnon
places.neighborhood: Place Baragnon and the old streets
places.note: Wednesday and Friday mornings, 08:00 to 13:00, tapenade, goat cheese, olives and linen up the streets behind the port; the Friday one is bigger, and neither happens on any other day.

places.name: Presqu'ile and the Port-Miou trailhead
places.neighborhood: West end of Cassis, avenue des Calanques
places.note: The start of the Calanques trail: 20 minutes from the port to the boat-lined inlet of Port-Miou and the viewpoint on the headland beyond it; the La Presqu'ile car park shuts in summer, so walk from town or take the Gorguettes shuttle.

places.name: Plage de la Grande Mer
places.note: The town beach next to the port, coarse sand mixed with pebbles and shallow water, 100m long and full by 10:30 in July; fine for a swim before dinner, not for a beach day.

places.name: Plage du Bestouan
places.note: Pebbles, a cold freshwater spring welling up in the sea, and the kayak hire for the calanques; locals prefer it to the Grande Mer, and the water is clearer.

places.name: Cap Canaille and the Route des Cretes
places.note: The 394m cliff road toward La Ciotat with lay-bys over the whole bay and the calanques beyond; closed to cars on Sundays and on red fire days and closed to everyone in a mistral above about 50 km/h, so check the barrier before you drive up.

places.name: Clos Sainte Magdeleine
places.neighborhood: Avenue du Revestel, below Cap Canaille
places.note: The prettiest of the dozen Cassis estates, vines running to the sea under the cliff, with a tasting of the white that Cassis is known for; open Monday to Saturday for sales and tastings by appointment, so phone the morning before.

places.name: Domaine du Paternel
places.note: A family estate with a cellar door open Monday to Saturday without an appointment, three whites and a rose from 12 euros a bottle; a 20 minute walk up from the port or a stop on the way in from the station.

places.name: Le Bonaparte
places.neighborhood: Rue du General Bonaparte, two streets back from the port
places.note: A family room away from the quay with grilled fish, aioli on Fridays and a plat du jour under 20 euros, cash preferred and shut on Sunday evening and Monday; the port restaurants 100m away charge double for the view.

places.name: La Poissonnerie Laurent
places.note: The fishmonger's own tables on the quay, sea urchins in season, grilled sardines and a fish soup; a straightforward lunch at 12:00 before the boats come in, and it closes some evenings and days in winter, so treat hours as loose.

places.name: La Villa Madie
places.neighborhood: Anse de Corton, east of the port
places.note: Three stars above a cove with a terrace over the water, tasting menus from roughly 180 euros at lunch to over 300 at dinner; closed Monday and Tuesday and for part of winter, and worth it only if a long lunch is the point of the day.

places.name: Chez Nino
places.note: The port's best-known fish restaurant since 1962, bouillabaisse and grilled bass on a first-floor terrace, 60 to 90 euros; solid, over-priced for what it is, and closed Sunday evening and Monday out of season.

places.name: Calanque de Port-Pin
places.note: Pine trees down to a 30m pebble beach in a narrow inlet, 45 minutes from the Cassis trailhead on an easy path; the one calanque you can do with children, and full by 11:00 in July.

places.name: Calanque d'En-Vau
places.note: The famous one, 100m walls and turquoise water at the bottom of a steep descent polished smooth by feet; pebbles, no shade, cold water, and shut on red fire days from June to September. Start by 08:00 and be back in Port-Pin by 14:00.

places.name: Calanque de Sugiton
places.note: Two pebble coves under the Candelle cliff 50 minutes below the Luminy bus stop, with a rope on the last drop; free permit from Troov required daily 27 June to 30 August, cap of 400 people, photo ID checked at the bottom.

places.name: Calanque de Morgiou
places.neighborhood: Calanques, from Luminy or the Morgiou road
places.note: A fishing hamlet with cabanons and one restaurant at the bottom of a valley, an hour down from Luminy; the road in is closed to cars 07:00 to 19:00 from mid-June to end August, and no permit is needed, which is why it is the fallback for Sugiton.

places.name: Calanque de Sormiou
places.note: The biggest beach in the park, sand and pebbles, with cabanons and a restaurant, reached by a road gated to cars in summer and a 45 minute walk down from the Col de Sormiou; bus 22 from Rond-Point du Prado to the gate.

places.name: Les Goudes and Callelongue
places.neighborhood: End of the Marseille coast road
places.note: The last village before the park, a fishing port of cabanons where bus 20 ends, with the Callelongue inlet 2km further and the Marseilleveyre trail starting there; lunch at the Grand Bar des Goudes or a sunset drink is what Marseille does on a Sunday.

places.name: Vieux Port fish market
places.note: A dozen fishermen's wives selling the night's catch off trestles from about 08:00 until it is gone, usually by 12:00; nothing to buy unless you are cooking, everything to see, and the mirrored canopy above is Norman Foster.

places.name: MuCEM and Fort Saint-Jean
places.neighborhood: J4, mouth of the Vieux Port
places.note: Rudy Ricciotti's concrete-lace cube joined by a footbridge to the 17th century fort, one ticket around 11 euros for every exhibition, the fort and the gardens free; 10:00 to 19:00 in summer and 18:00 in winter, closed Tuesdays, and the rooftop at sunset is the best free thing in the city.

places.name: Le Panier
places.note: The oldest quarter, a hill of narrow streets and painted walls above the port with the Vieille Charite's baroque chapel in the middle; it has gone from rough to boutiques in 15 years, and the place des Moulins at the top is still quiet.

places.name: Notre-Dame de la Garde
places.note: The striped basilica 150m over the city with a gold Virgin on top and model boats hanging from the ceiling, free, open about 07:00 to 19:00 with later hours in summer; bus 60 from the Vieux Port saves a 25 minute climb and the view covers If, Frioul and the Calanques.

places.name: Chez Fonfon
places.note: The bouillabaisse address since 1952 in a fishing inlet under the Corniche, open daily 12:00 to 14:00 and 19:00 to 22:00; the real thing is ordered for two the day before, around 95 to 100 euros a head with the rouille and the fish carved at the table, and the a la carte fish is half the price.

places.name: Chez Etienne
places.note: Wood-oven pizza half anchovy half cheese, supions with garlic and a beef pave in a room that has looked the same since 1943; no phone, no cards, no menu prices, about 25 euros a head and closed Sundays.

places.name: La Boite a Sardine
places.note: A fishmonger's canteen of tins, grilled sardines and whatever the boat had for 13 to 18 euros a plate, lunch only 12:00 to 14:30 Tuesday to Saturday; ten minutes' walk up from the Canebiere and full by 12:30.

places.name: Marche de Noailles and Maison Empereur
places.note: The Maghreb and Comorian market street behind the Canebiere, mint, spices, msemen and a sandwich for 4 euros, Monday to Saturday mornings; Maison Empereur on rue des Recolettes is the oldest hardware shop in France, since 1827, and better than any souvenir shop.

places.name: Cours Julien
places.note: The street-art square of bars, record shops and a Wednesday organic market, where a beer is 4 euros and the terraces run past midnight; a bit tired by daylight, right after 21:00, and the stairs down to Noailles are the way home.

places.name: Cite Radieuse, Le Corbusier
places.note: The 1952 concrete block of 337 flats on stilts with a shopping street on the third floor, a hotel and a rooftop gym now the MAMO art space; the lobby, the street and usually the roof are free to walk into, the tourist office runs guided tours of a flat for about 10 euros, and bus 21 or metro Rond-Po

places.name: Chateau d'If and the Frioul islands
places.neighborhood: Boats from the Vieux Port, quai des Belges
places.note: 20 minutes by boat to the prison of the Count of Monte Cristo, 7 euros and free under 26, open daily 10:00 to 18:00 in season and closed Mondays in winter, then on to Frioul for a swim in a limestone cove; the crossing is around 12 euros for If and 17 for both, and a mistral cancels everything.

places.name: Plage des Catalans
places.note: The nearest sand to the Vieux Port, 15 minutes on foot, a small city beach with volleyball nets and a 1 euro entry gate some summers; Marseille's own beach rather than a resort, and the Prado beaches further south are imported sand and gravel.
